messages:
Ajay G: heads up — we had a spike in preemptible GPU evictions in us-west-2 last night, sustained ~18% reclaim rate for ~45m, caused tail latency > SLO for realtime routes. anyone digging in?
Maria L: saw the alert, grafana shows eviction spikes aligning with market price jumps at 02:12-02:50 UTC. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/di/evictions/spot-usw2 (perm only)
Taylor: looks like the price-optimized pools got thin and AWS started reclaiming cheaper capacity. our capacity-optimized pools stayed up but we didn't route enough traffic to them.
Vikram: agree. price-optimized minimizes cost but increases p(eviction). we should try a small experiment mixing pools with a simple scoring function instead of hard fallback.
Ajay G: proposal: primary routing -> capacity-optimized (70%), overflow -> price-optimized (30%) with graceful fallback. Also add a small warm buffer of reserved nodes for headroom.
Maria L: preliminary numbers: switching 30% to capacity-optimized in a dev cluster last week dropped evictions 60% but monthly GPU spend rose ~12%. tradeoffs expected.
Taylor: technical notes: make sure we do 3 things on routing change — 1) set drain_timeout for spot preempts, 2) push checkpoint frequency earlier for long jobs, 3) increase KV cache TTL to avoid cold-start churn on fallback.
Vikram: example rollout snippet for the autoscaler (pseudo):
```yaml
pools:
  - name: capacity-optimized-primary
    strategy: capacity-optimized
    weight: 0.7
  - name: price-optimized-overflow
    strategy: price-optimized
    weight: 0.3
warm_buffer:
  nodes: 6
  ttl: 5m
drain_timeout: 120s
```
Ajay G: can we also add a simple score function for preferring pools per-request? e.g. score = alpha*(1 - p_eviction) + beta*(1 - cost_norm) where p_eviction is recent 10m eviction rate.
Taylor: yeah, store per-pool eviction_rate and recent_price in TSDB and compute score per-minute. start with alpha=0.7 beta=0.3 and tune.
Maria L: need telemetry: interruption_rate, reclaim_latency (time between spot eviction signal and GPU unavailability), request_fails_during_fallback. I can add panels.
Vikram: ops checklist for experiment:
- canary 10% traffic for 24h
- 70/30 weight in canary
- automatic fallback policy: if reclaim_rate(pool) > 15% for 10m, shift 20% away
- alert: reclaim_rate > 25% triggers rollback
Ajay G: what about region fallback? if primary region loses capacity we should avoid big cross-region egress spikes. prefer nearby region with lower egress cost first.
Taylor: add region_penalty to score (distance + egress cost). sample: score -= region_penalty*0.2.
Maria L: FYI some customers require strict region pinning — for those we should keep policy price-optimized only within allowed region, and rely on higher reserved/warm buffer.
Vikram: operational flags to enable for canary:
- enable_pool_mixing: true
- canary_ratio: 0.1
- score_weights: {alpha:0.7,beta:0.3,region_penalty:0.2}
Ajay G: i'll open a runbook and the PR for autoscaler changes. want SRE to watch the canary and rollback if we see tail latencies.
capacity-bot: Autoscaler: canary rollout started for pool-mix experiment (id: pmix-2026-07-20), targeting 10% traffic in us-west-2.
Taylor: nice. small ask — add logging for "eviction_reason" tag so we can disambiguate price vs capacity signals.
Maria L: will add panels and the logs query. also adding a cost delta forecast for the 72h window so finance can see the impact.
Ajay G: great — plan: run 48h canary, baseline metrics (eviction_rate, p95 latency, unit_gpu_cost). if eviction_rate drops >40% and p95 within SLO, we'll ramp to 50/50.
Vikram: will prepare the canary playbook and the rollback steps.
Taylor: :+1:
Maria L: :eyes: monitoring ready, will tag the alert channel.
Ajay G: thanks team — looping in @oncall if anything fires during the night.
capacity-bot: DeployBot: autoscaler config change merged to canary branch (commit: 9f2ad3).
